chapter: Leaving Hampton and starting his own band
title: Dutch Kitchen Bounce, Bob Causer's credit and refusing outside publishers
summary: Cobb explains how Cornell's Bob Causer got title credit for two tunes, and why he refused to let another publisher control Dutch Kitchen Bounce after being cheated over Tempo and Swing.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: : No. Well now, okay, so you've got this band, and you work seven months. Now, what is happening that you got into the hospital?

Well, let's get back to the record first, STANLEY (Inaudible). I had -- I didn't have a title to "Dutch Kitchen BOUNCE." I didn't have a title to Go, Red, Go. They were just numbers that we played, and they're my original numbers, because Bootie Woods was with me on Dutch Kitchen BOUNCE, and we wrote that together.

Bob Causer, who was the owner of the Ithaca Hotel in Ithaca, New York, and had a swank eating joint on Cornell University campus called Dutch Kitchen Inn, he came up to my recording session on the first day, and he was a guy who liked, would -- with "St. Vitus Dance," you know. And I was almost -- you know, I was feeling sorry for him, and I was in

bad shape myself. My back was still bothering me, you know, but he wanted -- claim writer and title of these tunes for his situation up there. I said, 'Very good.' He said, 'I don't want no money for it.' He said, 'Just put me on the record as a writer of these two tunes.' He said, 'Now, name this one -- I got the Dutch Kitchen Inn,' and he said, 'You know, Cornell's pep yell is Go, Red, Go.'"
Did he get royalties on it?
No, he didn't get anything. He didn't want anything. All he wanted -- they're going to play it on the campus.

And he wanted the prestige in it. That's what he wanted. And I followed that, and I thought BOUGHT that. But what he did, he come to me, and they wanted Sarah to do Dutch Kitchen BOUNCE and have somebody to do the lyrics on it to the title, to the melody. But he wanted to publishing company bring me in and let another publisher come in and handle it, and I said, 'No, indeed. I am the controller of this one. I've been through this already with Lionel Hampton with 'Tempo and Swing.' I don't want nobody to have none of my tunes no more and treating me like they want to treat me about it. If I never get any lyrics to Dutch Kitchen BOUNCE,' it would be

too soon, when it got to go that way.
And that's where I drew the line. I went along with Bob on what he wanted, but when he wanted some lyrics and put Sarah Vaughan on it, good, but let me still control it with Wayne Music Publishing Company. That's mine. But he wanted Mills or somebody downtown in New York. No way. No way. I've been ripped off too much, and I'm tired of being ripped off. I'd take it and let it die before I'd let somebody make more money off of my own material than I could make off of it, and that's what they're going to do to me.
Why do you think he wanted to have that moved to Mills? How What would that benefit him?
Don't ask me because I don't know what people are talking behind my back.
(Inaudible) amount of money they're going to spend to push it. They're going to take it as merchandise and work on it. (inaudible) that money
And I have no control of keeping of accounting -- I was being sold on it. And they make the money.
